findings.message: Await the registration check before allowing check-in. `isRegistered` is asynchronous, so this condition negates a truthy Promise and never enters the rejection branch. Scanning any existing participant therefore checks them into the event even when they have no registration. Await the result before testing it.

Call hooks before the conditional return. The parent keeps this component mounted while toggling `isOpen`, but this return skips `useTuyau` and `useForm` whenever the dialog is closed. Closing it after opening changes the hook sequence, violating React's hook ordering and potentially producing hook-count errors or leaving form effects mounted. Move the return below all hooks, or conditionally mount the entire component in the parent.

Show the scanner independently of staff registration status. The scanner trigger is nested inside `!isRegistered`, so staff members who have registered for an event cannot open its check-in scanner. Staff can also have participant profiles and register through the existing route. Render the staff scanner trigger outside the registration-button condition so those staff members can still check attendees in.
